svg.title: CH347T (TSSOP20) pinout by mode, from WCH CH347DS1 V1.6
svg.text: Each pin's function in modes 1/2, 0 and 3. atiic uses mode 1: I2C and SPI on a vendor interface (1a86:55db).
Modes: pins 10 (DTR1) and 13 (RTS1), read at reset (both pulled up inside: open = high)
two serial ports (UART0 with all modem lines, UART1 with some)
UART1 + I2C + SPI on a vendor interface (WebUSB): atiic
UART1 + I2C + SPI as HID, no driver (WebHID)
• VCC wants 3.3 V from outside (0.1 uF to ground); the I/O run at 3.3 V, the 5V-marked inputs take 5 V.
• Modes 1/2: SDA and SCL have pull-ups inside. ACT goes low once USB is configured.
• A pull-down on ACT at power-up turns DTR1 into TNOW1 (RS485 enable); on DTR0 (mode 0), DTR0 and DTR1 both.
• A pull-down on RTS0 (pin 7, mode 0) at power-up: the chip ignores its EEPROM settings and runs on its defaults.
• No series resistors on UD+ / UD−. GPIO names as the datasheet's pin tables give them (modes 0 and 3).
Source: WCH CH347DS1 V1.6, §4.3 (tables 4-8 to 4-12) and §5.2. atiic docs/ch347.md.
